reflexion_entries_to_archive.text: S137 P0b: the handoff, and my own static chain, both blamed the hunter bench for a swallowed click -- but the failure snapshot showed tick 261 against a ~400-tick catch, so the inference looked WRONG and I nearly went hunting for a second cause. Adding one diagnostic to the throw (all three isInputLocked clauses, printed individually) settled it in a single run: lockedByBench=true, benchedUntilTick=1925 at tick 330, hunters already empty. The estimate was stale, not the theory. When a failure message names a SYMPTOM ("panel did not open") rather than a CAUSE, the cheapest next move is almost never more reading -- it is making the failure say why. Cost: ~30 lines. Saved: an open-ended hunt.

S137 P0a: fog.spec asserted aboveFogLayer.children.length === 13. When it became 14 the failure said "Expected 13 / Received 14" and nothing else, and attributing the extra child cost an entire prior session. Replacing the count with an ORDERED CONSTRUCTOR-NAME list (each line commented with its owning renderer) makes the diff point at the index that moved, and catches what a count structurally cannot -- one renderer leaking a second child while another adds none still sums to 14. Rule: if a test pins a NUMBER that stands for a LIST, pin the list. Also: I MEASURED the expected list (deliberate failing assertion printed the received array) rather than writing what I believed, and the measured Container positions then independently confirmed the static attribution.

S137 A.0: a one-line regex count of PLAYER_COLORS returned 9 because it split on commas inside the block COMMENTS. I was one step from reporting "e2e/helpers.ts hardcodes /7 but there are 9 seats -- the keep geometry is broken", a confident and completely wrong finding. Reading the declaration directly showed 7. A measurement that is cheap to take is not automatically safe to trust; for anything that will become a CLAIM, read the source of truth rather than a derived count.
